title: The eligible-medication list and the separate legal texts it rests on
subtopic: Eligible medications and their legal bases
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 states that the following generic medications, which may have multiple brand names, are the only medications eligible to be administered by a pharmacist or pharmacy intern. Long-acting injectable antipsychotics: aripiprazole, aripiprazole lauroxil, fluphenazine decanoate, haloperidol decanoate, paliperidone palmitate, risperidone and risperidone ER. Long-acting injectable medications for substance use disorders: buprenorphine and naltrexone. Gender-affirming care medications: testosterone (all salts). HIV prevention medications: cabotegravir, and lenacapavir (or other medications to prevent HIV). Sexually transmitted infection medications: ceftriaxone (IM injection), and doxycycline (or other medications to treat chlamydia). The circular states that there is no requirement for pharmacists or pharmacy interns to administer these medications, and that in accordance with 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) and this Department guidance pharmacists and pharmacy interns are authorized to administer certain medications for treating mental illness and substance use disorder, testosterone for gender-affirming care, antiviral therapy for prevention of HIV, and antibiotics for the treatment and prevention of sexually transmitted infections, citing M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1. 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) itself reaches FDA approved mental health or substance use disorder treatment drugs, and 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(d)1. requires the Department's guidelines to include requirements for the specific drugs permitted to be administered pursuant to 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9). The definition of Administer in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1, clause (c)(ii) and (iii), separately reaches a registered pharmacist acting in accordance with a prescription for testosterone for gender-affirming care, or a prescription for the treatment and prevention of sexually transmitted infections or for the prevention of HIV.
exam_relevance: Tests that the list is exhaustive and stated by generic name, that eligibility does not oblige anyone to administer, and that the regulation's words reach the mental health and substance use disorder drugs while the statute separately names prescriptions for testosterone for gender-affirming care and for sexually transmitted infections and HIV prevention.

exceptions: Two entries extend beyond a named generic medication: lenacapavir (or other medications to prevent HIV) and doxycycline (or other medications to treat chlamydia).
Testosterone is listed in all salts.
common_confusions: Treating the list as examples of a broader class of injectables.
Rejecting a medication because its brand name does not appear, when the list is stated by generic name.
Attributing the testosterone, HIV prevention and sexually transmitted infection categories to 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9), whose words reach mental health or substance use disorder treatment drugs.
Describing the circular as Board of Registration in Pharmacy guidance, when it describes itself as Department guidance.
Assuming a listed medication must be administered on request.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-14 in Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, dated March 11, 2026 (the Word document linked from the Department's news page on mass.gov), in the current text of 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) on mass.gov, and in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 on malegislature.gov.
